## D — Accuracy notes and source flags: safety belts, child restraints and air bags
Every C and C2 fact cites exactly one physical manual page from the selected range; nothing relies on outside knowledge.
The whole manual carries an old content-currency date (stated in part A), so any rule here may have changed since; the freshness debt in part A covers every fact in this section.
The back-seat belt rule is internally inconsistent: it covers passengers under seventeen but says it stops applying only at eighteen or older, leaving seventeen-year-olds unclear; only the under-seventeen wording is taught (verify TN-BELT-D-AGE) [A01].
The unattended-child penalty conflicts across two pages: one page gives a fine-only Class B misdemeanor [A03], while the next says leaving a child unattended can be charged anywhere from a Class A misdemeanor to a Class A felony [A04]; only the fine-only statute version is taught, and the separate child abuse penalties are taught as their own law (verify TN-BELT-D-UNATTENDED).
The crash and survival statistics are figures the manual quotes from national and state sources for past years; they are taught as attributed to the manual and are not refreshed here [A02].
The air bag lives-saved figure is an old NHTSA estimate quoted by the manual and is taught only as the manual's attributed claim [A03].

corpus_stability.reason: The Tennessee Comprehensive Driver License Manual says its content is current as of July 1, 2022 and its back cover carries one March 2025 print authorization; nothing in the selected pages suggests more than one rewrite per year, but the content date is old, so freshness is held as debt rather than assumed.

verification_debt.claim_text: Physical page 45 requires belts for back-seat passengers under 17 but says the rule no longer applies once they are 18 or older, leaving 17-year-olds unclear; confirm the current back-seat belt age.

Physical page 47 makes leaving a child under 7 unattended a Class B misdemeanor punishable only by a 200 or 500 dollar fine, while physical page 48 says the penalty can range from a Class A misdemeanor to a Class A felony; confirm which charges apply.
